claims.text: Oxidation resistance and material integrity in high-temperature MPEAs are governed by their ability to form a continuous, adherent, slow-growing protective oxide scale.
Selective enrichment of chromium or aluminum promotes formation of the protective oxide scale.
The protective oxide scale limits oxygen diffusion and slows further oxidation.
Slower oxidation caused by the protective scale preserves bulk material integrity.
The proposed initial material is a solid-solution MPEA with a balanced distribution of reactive elements such as Cr, Al, and possibly Si.
The controlled intervention is sustained exposure to a high-temperature oxidizing environment at constant oxygen partial pressure.
Representative harsh-service test temperatures range from approximately 800 to 1200°C.
The relevant structural mediator is a dense, adherent surface layer such as Cr2O3 or Al2O3.
Selective oxidation of Cr or Al forms a protective scale that retards oxidation by restricting oxygen diffusion.
Insufficient reactive-element content produces a less effective protective scale and consequently accelerated oxidation and degradation.
A microstructure that does not promote rapid selective oxidation produces a less effective protective scale and consequently accelerated oxidation and degradation.
Alloys forming continuous and adherent protective scales will have lower oxidation rates than comparable alloys that do not form such scales.
Alloys forming continuous and adherent protective scales will retain mechanical integrity better than comparable alloys without such scales.
Relative to the conventional-alloy baseline, the proposed MPEAs should exhibit delayed oxidation onset.
Relative to the conventional-alloy baseline, the proposed MPEAs should exhibit less scale spallation or cracking.
Relative to the conventional-alloy baseline, the proposed MPEAs should exhibit lower mass gain per unit area over time.
The hypothesis is expected to apply to well-mixed MPEAs under oxidizing conditions from approximately 800 to 1200°C.
The proposed controlled comparison uses MPEAs with high versus reduced Cr and/or Al concentrations under otherwise identical oxidation conditions.
Mass gain, scale thickness, continuity, phase composition, and pre/post-exposure mechanical properties can distinguish the proposed behaviors.
Failure of the high-reactive-element samples to show lower mass gain, a more continuous and adherent scale, and better mechanical-property retention than controls would falsify the hypothesis.
